item.title: Two-thirds of women in NL feel unheard by healthcare workers
item.description:
Two-thirds of women in NL feel unheard by healthcare workers

October 12, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Two-thirds of women in the Netherlands say they don’t always feel heard by healthcare professionals, for example when describing symptoms, asking for referrals or discussing treatment options, according to a new report by polling company Kieskompas.

The findings were sent to MPs today and drawn from a survey of 14,000 women aged 16 and over. Only one in five women in the survey said healthcare professionals listen well to women.

Women aged 25 to 54 and women with unexplained symptoms were the most likely to say they felt misunderstood by consultants, and fewer than half of women with a condition or disability said the care they received helped them sufficiently.

Women also said they felt less well informed about topics that only affect women, such as menopause, than about general health issues. Women of all ages said they wanted that information, and would like to see more research on it.

According to ZonMw, a research funding body behind the report, girls would like to know more about how hormones can impact mental health for example.

Nearly two in three women said they thought women did not feel comfortable discussing health problems at work. Of women with health problems, 63% said these had affected their work, mainly through stress and lower productivity, and over a quarter had stopped working earlier than planned.

A second report, also presented on Monday, analysed the experiences of women who have got stuck in the healthcare system because of long-term, unexplained symptoms. The analysis, carried out by health research institute Nivel for the Voices for Women foundation, was based on surveys and accounts that women submitted themselves, which the researchers note it is not representative.

A lack of recognition came up in almost every account, ANP reported, and only one in four women said they felt heard by their care provider. According to ZonMw, almost 90% did not feel taken seriously, and 65% said they often got a psychological diagnosis when they came in with a physical complaint.

“The two new reports underline the urgency of the message ZonMw and others have been spreading for some time: more attention for women’s health is needed,” ZonMw said in a statement.

item.title: Two NSC MPs join exodus as Keijzer triggers conference walkout
item.description:
Two NSC MPs join exodus as Keijzer triggers conference walkout

October 12, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Two former MPs for New Social Contract have resigned in protest at the party’s decision to invite right-wing independent MP Mona Keijzer to a weekend conference.

Harm Holman, NSC’s former agriculture spokesman, and Ilse Saris, who covered social affairs, said they no longer felt at home in a party that was drifting towards right-wing populism.

Saturday’s general meeting in Breda ended in chaos when the party’s entire management board resigned following a mass walkout when Keijzer stepped up onto the stage. Acting chairman Ronald de Bruin said the situation had become “untenable” after around half the delegates left the room.

Keijzer had been invited to discuss her hardline conservative movement, Project 2029, which she launched after breaking from the farmers’ party BBB earlier this year.

Holman told TV late night news show Nieuwsuur: “NSC was a reasonable centre party in terms of its policies, but it has becoming a populist party that is moving further to the right. I don’t feel at home there.”

Saris said in a parting note: “In my eyes the party has completely departed from what NSC stood for.”

Een walk-out bij het NSC-congres het moment dat @MonaKeijzer het woord neemt. Vooraf was er al veel consternatie over Keijzer als gastspreker. Het was voor @DirkGotink reden om uit de partij te stappen. Nu loopt de helft de zaal uit https://t.co/4PD2YoYwfn

— Nouschka van der Meijden (@NouschkavdM) October 10, 2026

The decision by NSC’s management  board to invite Keijzer as a guest speaker prompted its last elected parliamentarian, MEP Dirk Gotink, to resign his membership.

Gotink, 45, said in a post on LinkedIn that seeking closer ties with Keijzer was “incomprehensible”, despite the NSC leadership insisting that there was no agreement to work with her.

Voters return to CDA

NSC won 20 seats in the November 2023 election, just three months after being founded by Omtzigt, who recruited many of his candidates from his old party, the Christian Democrats (CDA).

But the party’s support collapsed soon after Omtzigt joined the right-wing coalition with Geert Wilders’ far-right PVV, the right-wing liberal VVD and the BBB the following year.

Wilders blamed NSC for blocking his plans to introduce the “harshest immigration policy ever”, while Omtzigt resigned first as party leader and then as an MP, citing the toll on his health and family life.

Many of NSC’s voters reverted to the CDA at the election last October, while NSC itself was wiped out. Holman, 69, also said at the weekend that he had rejoined the Christian Democrats.

item.title: One-way traffic on IJssel river lifted but “drought is not over”
item.description:
One-way traffic on IJssel river lifted but “drought is not over”

October 12, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

The highways agency Rijkswaterstaat has lifted restrictions on the IJssel river that forced ships carrying freight from Arnhem to Zutphen to take a 300km detour.

A one-way system was imposed on September 24 after the river level dropped as a result of the summer drought both in the Netherlands and further upstream in Germany and Switzerland.

The agency said it was able to allow ships to travel in both directions now that the water level has risen to 1.45m above its baseline, but it warned that the drought period is “not over”.

Koninklijke Binnnenvaart Nederland, which represents inland waterway users, said the ending of the restriction was welcome, but shipping operators were still having to contend with limitations such as transporting lighter loads.

“The problems are not over. Low water is still having a big impact on inland shipping,” a spokesman said.

item.title: “Many Dutch adults can only swim one stroke”
item.description:
“Many Dutch adults can only swim one stroke”

October 12, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Former junior Romanian swimming champion Vlad Pațurcă moved to the Netherlands alone at the age of 21. Since then he’s founded his own swimming school in Amsterdam-Noord, where he now coaches hundreds of people. He idolises former Dutch Olympic swimming champions and dreams of one day building a squad of competitive swimmers.

How did you end up in the Netherlands?
I was a competitive swimmer in Romania, a freestyle sprinter, and swam for the youth national team. In 2021 I visited the Netherlands for the first time. The first city I saw wasn’t Amsterdam but Assen, in the north, and I fell for the Dutch way of life straight away: the quiet, the order, the way everything seemed designed for people. After that I didn’t want to be anywhere else.

I moved here at 21, with little work experience and no idea how Dutch law or business worked, and started coaching at a large adult swim club. In my first months there I saw how many adults wanted lessons. In 2024 I opened my own swim school, Win and Swim, in Amsterdam-Noord.

I paid for the first pool lane out of my own pocket and started with five or six swimmers. Since then we’ve taught more than 300 adults.

How do you describe yourself – an expat, lovepat, immigrant, international?
An international. The Netherlands is home now. Many of the people I teach are internationals too, often adults learning to swim from scratch.

How long do you plan to stay?
For good. I’ve built my business here and the plan is to grow it: more hours and new locations in Amsterdam first, then children’s lessons and other Dutch cities.
My dream is a performance squad, where I train competitive swimmers. Besides the swim school, I help companies with AI solutions.

Do you speak Dutch and how did you learn?
Not yet, and that’s a real challenge when you run a business. So far I’ve run Win and Swim almost entirely in English, and I’m learning Dutch now so I can take the business further.

In my first years here I did A1 through a free government course while I was living in Almere. After I moved to Amsterdam I wanted to continue with A2, but the free places go first to newcomers who need the lessons to integrate, for example to find work. I was already working and settled here, so I wasn’t in that group.

What’s your favourite Dutch thing?
My favourite thing is that things just work. When I opened my company, I entered my details online at the KVK chamber of commerce, went in the next day to sign and that was it: the company was open.

In Romania I’d have been running from one office to another, printing and signing papers. Here, sorting something out at the bank or the council is just as easy.

How Dutch have you become?
Dutch enough to appreciate the directness. People had told me the Dutch are cold. They’re not cold, just very direct, and at first that felt harsh. Now I value that nobody beats around the bush and nobody makes promises they don’t keep.

Which three Dutch people (dead or alive) would you most like to meet?
Pieter van den Hoogenband, Inge de Bruijn and Maarten van der Weijden. The first two are freestyle sprint legends, and sprint freestyle was my event. Van der Weijden came back from leukaemia to win Olympic open-water gold in 2008.

What’s your top tourist tip?
In summer, swim outdoors, but only at an official swimming spot (zwemlocatie), where the water quality is checked. Het Twiske, just north of Amsterdam-Noord, is a good one. And get on a bike. Here people of every age and every job cycle every day, and it’s the best way to see the country.

Tell us something surprising you’ve found out about the Netherlands.
Almost everyone here learned to swim as a child: around 94% of Dutch youngsters hold at least one swimming diploma. You’d expect a country of strong swimmers, but the reality is more nuanced. Many Dutch adults can only swim one stroke, breaststroke with the head out of the water.

The system teaches survival rather than swimming as a sport, which makes sense in a country full of canals. As a result, many Dutch adults come back to lessons later to learn freestyle and the other strokes.

If you had just 24 hours left in the Netherlands, what would you do?
Spend the day on my bike, out of the city, and end it with one last swim.

Vlad was speaking with Louis Gore-Langton

item.title: Jetten condemns planned US sanctions against ICC, urges dialogue
item.description:
Jetten condemns planned US sanctions against ICC, urges dialogue

October 12, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Dutch prime minister Rob Jetten has condemned the United States’ decision to impose sanctions on the International Criminal Court in The Hague and said the Netherlands would defend the institution “brick by brick”.

In a joint press conference with Antonio Costa, president of the European Council, Jetten said the announcement by Secretary of State Marco Rubio on Friday was “deeply regrettable”. He went on: “We’re very much disappointed by this escalation and condemn the announced sanctions.”

Jetten said the next six months would be a “crucial” time after the Trump administration delayed the onset of the measures to allow “time for states parties to demonstrate meaningful progress on diplomatic and legal resolutions that address fundamental US concerns regarding the ICC.”

Rubio said the court was a threat to American servicemen who faced being prosecuted for their actions during overseas missions, even though the United States is not a member.

The US has also attacked the decision to serve arrest warrants on Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu and former defence minister Yoav Gallant.

“We will ban transactions with this rogue court, cutting off their resources and crippling its ability to operate,” he said.

Nobel Prize

The announcement came hours after South African jurist Navi Pillay, who has served as a judge at both the ICC and the International Court of Justice in The Hague, was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize.

Jetten called for “open dialogue” with the US over the next six months “to prevent the sanctions being implemented in April”, but he added: “At the same time we are preparing for a more difficult situation.”

He would not say if the Netherlands, as the host of the ICC, would ask the European Union to activate its blocking statute, ordering EU-based businesses not to comply with the sanctions, but he said: “We will do everything to protect the ICC.”

The sanctions will cut the court off from any US company or organisation, including providers of financial and technology services. They are the first measures to be announced against the institution rather than individual staff members.

The Trump administration has so far sanctioned 13 judges and officials at the ICC, including the court’s president, Tomoko Akane, and senior prosecutor Abdoulaye Saye, preventing them from travelling to the US or using banking services.

item.title: D66 wants children heard without parents’ consent in abuse cases
item.description:
D66 wants children heard without parents’ consent in abuse cases

October 12, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Children who show serious signs of abuse would be interviewed quickly, and without their parents’ consent if necessary, under a draft bill published by coalition party D66 on Monday.

The proposal, by MPs Marijke Synhaeve and Hanneke van der Werf, has been put online so organisations can respond before it goes to parliament, broadcaster NOS reported. “What we want,” Synhaeve said, “is for children to be better heard, seen and helped.”

Currently, care workers can normally only contact a child if the parents or guardians agree. Exceptions are possible under strict conditions, but they are complicated and rarely used. Recent serious abuse cases have led leaders to consider altering policies.

Under what the MPs call the “child first act”, a specialist team would have to hear the child within 48 hours when there are signs of a criminal offence.

The team would include medical, youth care, safety and justice experts, and would draw up a plan covering protection, support and, if needed, prosecution.

The approach is based on the Barnahus model, Icelandic for “children’s house”, which is already used in many other countries.

Missed signals
D66 first announced the plan in June, citing two cases in which children’s calls for help went unanswered. The foster parents of a 10-year-old girl in Vlaardingen were jailed for 8 years last November for abuse that left her permanently disabled.

Government inspectors found that the girl had made several efforts to get help but was ignored.

In May, two women in the Groningen town of Stadskanaal were arrested on suspicion of severely abusing a 6-year-old girl and a 7-year-old boy. In both cases, signals from the children or people around them were not properly followed up, NOS said.

A majority of MPs backed similar ideas during a recent debate on domestic violence, news agency ANP reported in June. Far-right JA21 MP Ingrid Coenradie also put forward the same idea in that debate.

Synhaeve said she does not expect the bill to create a lot of extra work or lead to more children being taken into care. She said it would instead improve cooperation between agencies.

item.title: Fire that damaged cables under railway bridge is suspected arson
item.description:
Fire that damaged cables under railway bridge is suspected arson

October 12, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Police are investigating a fire under a railway bridge in Rotterdam that led to trains being cancelled over the weekend as a suspected act of sabotage.

The door to a technical area in Rotterdam-Delfshaven was forced open and a fire was started that damaged around 35 cables, 15 of which were destroyed, network operator ProRail said.

All trains between Rotterdam Centraal and Delft Campus were suspended until 9.15pm on Sunday as engineers worked to repair the damage.

The stretch of line is one of the busiest in the Netherlands, carrying long-distance trains from Amsterdam to Zeeland and Limburg via Holland Spoor station.

A police spokesman told Dutch News: “We have secured camera footage and we are examining it. Forensic investigators are also studying possible leads.”

Junior infrastructure minister Annet Bertram said she was shocked by the incident. “I find it appalling and worrying that this appears to be arson and a deliberate act,” she told NOS.

Schiphol disruption

In a separate incident, trains to Schiphol airport were disrupted for several hours by problems with an overhead power line, but ProRail has ruled out arson as a cause.

More than 20 sprinter trains between Amsterdam and Hoofddorp were cancelled between 1.30pm and 9pm as engineers worked to repair the fault at Riekerpolder. “It is an intersection, which means trains are not running in a large area,” a spokesman said on Sunday.

International services were also affected, with trains to Brussels starting and ending in Rotterdam.

item.title: Utrecht weighs tougher measures on landlords after lack of fines
item.description:
Utrecht weighs tougher measures on landlords after lack of fines

October 12, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Utrecht fined only 1 landlord last year despite receiving almost 200 complaints for breaking rules designed to protect tenants. The city is now considering a tougher approach modelled on Rotterdam, which issued 25 penalties in the second half of the year alone.

The figures were reported by regional broadcaster RTV Utrecht. Rotterdam received 667 complaints in 2025, and its fines ranged from €1,000 to tens of thousands per offence.

The threat of a fine is often enough to resolve a dispute since many renters are too scared to even report illegal or abusive practice for fear of losing their homes amid the housing crisis, but the city showed that when tenants did make reports, rents fell an average of €350 for private tenants.

Under the “good landlord law”, which came into force in 2023, landlords cannot discriminate against or intimidate tenants. Deposits are capped at 2 months’ basic rent, and service charges may only cover actual costs.

Unlike Rotterdam, Utrecht gives landlords a warning before handing down a penalty. It says it wants to avoid having fines overturned in court for being too heavy.

Research published by the Federation of Private-Sector Tenants (FHCS) in December last year found that Utrecht lacked the resources to look for abuses itself and relied entirely on complaints from tenants. Only around half of those complaints were taken further, usually because of a lack of evidence.

Fines are also rare in other big cities. In The Hague, around 600 complaints in two and a half years led to dozens of penalty orders but only 3 fines, which are being contested, according to the FHCS.

Amsterdam’s public list of sanctions showed only 1 fine, for intimidating tenants, which could still be challenged. Last October, the city warned a landlord who would only rent to working Dutch women that he faced a fine of up to €10,000.

Utrecht has not yet decided whether to follow Rotterdam’s lead, but believes fines could deter landlords and prevent repeat offences. It aims to introduce a rental permit in 2028, so that rents can be checked before a home is let.

The city also plans to do more to inform tenants about their rights and its complaints hotline. Every council is required by law to run a hotline for complaints about landlords.

item.title: Feyenoord top Eredivisie as AZ left seething over denied penalty
item.description:
Feyenoord top Eredivisie as AZ left seething over denied penalty

October 12, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Feyenoord climbed to the top of the Eredivisie after a 2-0 win over AZ Alkmaar took them above their opponents for the first time this season.

Nacho Ferri continued his strong start to the season by putting the Rotterdammers ahead in the 13th minute as he capitalised on a poor defensive header by Wouter Goes.

Fellow Spaniard Javi López scored the second from a corner in the second half to make sure of the points.

Coach Giovanni van Bronkhorst played down the significance of the result, telling NOS: “We have a long way to go and need to keep both feet on the ground.”

AZ were aggrieved that they were denied a penalty just before half-time when Mexx Meerdink appeared to have been brought down by Tjark Ernst.

Meerdink called the decision by referee Danny Makkelie “disgraceful”, but coach Leeroy Echteld refused to linger on the incident. “I’m not interested in being dragged into that kind of story,” he said.

PSV blank

PSV kept their first clean sheet of the season to beat Heerenveen 2-0 in the Friday night game, but the result owed much to the visitors’ wastefulness in front of goal.

Guus Til, playing as a stand-in striker, headed in the first after half an hour after good work by Esmir Bajraktarevic on the right wing, while the second was an own goal by Marcus Linday.

Twente and Fortuna Sittard, two teams enjoying strong starts to the season, shared the points in Enschede. Anthony Descotte headed in an inswinging cross by Mo Ihattaren to give Fortuna the lead in the ninth minute, before Robin Pröpper tapped in the equaliser before half-time.

Ajax stay fifth after they had to settle for a point against NEC Nijmegen. Tjaronn Chery equalised for NEC from the penalty spot after Tolu Arokodare had given the hosts an early lead.

Groningen hit five

Groningen put on a dominant second-half display to win 5-1 at Excelsior, but the turning point came at the end of the first period when Excelsior goalkeeper Stijn van Gessel fumbled a cross by Tika de Jonge into his own net.

Go Ahead Eagles and Sparta shared six goals in Deventer, but only after Sparta’s Andrej Kostic squandered a golden chance for a last-minute winner when he blasted the ball over the crossbar.

Utrecht managed their second win under coach Anthony Correia thanks to two outstanding goals by Yoanne Cathline against Willem II, while a late Nicholas Bindner goal earned Cambuur their first away win of the season at PEC Zwolle.

Telstar played most of their match against ADO Den Haag with an extra man following the dismissal of Milan Hokke in the 13th minute, but still only managed a draw as Tyrone Owusu scored twice.

item.title: Albert Heijn app and deliveries down after “IT incident”
item.description:
Albert Heijn app and deliveries down after “IT incident”

October 12, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Albert Heijn has been hit by an “IT incident” according to a company statement released on Monday morning, which notes that cosmetics chain Etos and alcohol shop Gall and Gall are also affected. All three chains are owned by Ahold Delhaize.

Albert Heijn has switched off part of its IT systems, leaving its website, app and home delivery service unavailable.

“We immediately took measures to protect our IT environment,” the company said in a statement on Monday. “Part of that is temporarily switching off a number of systems as a precaution.” Customer services and logistics systems are offline, and online order cannot be delivered until further notice.

AH has not said what caused the incident or when services will return. It said only that protecting the data of customers, staff and partners is its priority.

Shops are open and tills are working, but personal discounts and app-linked savings schemes are paused. Electronic shelf labels may also show last week’s offer prices, the chain said, so the prices at the till can be higher than shown on shelves.
